notes: Same full 5,032,104-document fixture, all 962 official and 714 supplemental queries, four commands, seven rotated complete-pass samples after ten-second warmup per engine/command, CPU 2 for both driver and engines. This additional runner does not silently replace the upstream benchmark protocol.

Selected source and candidate use the same immutable rounded index and compiler/flags. Tantivy binary and index match the preceding verified controls. The candidate changes only scoring.rs over the archived selected source; no format, ranking-model or query-list route changes.

Candidate single-essential windows append decoded scored runs directly, preserving existing windows, pruning, predicates and exact canonical contributions. Multiple essential cursors retain dense union materialization; both share one run visitor and scorer.

Fresh candidate gates cover all 1676 queries on rounded and group indexes: COUNT against Tantivy, top-10/100/1000 against exhaustive scoring, and complete cross-source ordered top-1000 IDs/score bits/count against verified V4. Local ARM canonical and merged fixtures pass the same independent oracles.

No new WASM build for native performance iterations, per the user instruction. Native tests, Clippy, raw ARM samples, process memory, immutable-byte manifests, cloud software profiles and validated nonempty address-range disassembly are retained.

All indexing, compilation, correctness gates, profiling, large transfers and hash verification occur outside latency measurement. Software annotation is not hardware-cycle attribution; any unsuccessful annotation is recorded explicitly.
Exact duplicate files are stored once; restore_aliases.py recreates and verifies every original logical path. Binaries and raw perf data remain in the separately hashed full archive.
Warm single-query comparisons do not establish cold-cache, concurrent-ingest, sparse-index or overall search-engine superiority.
